about.title: La Mirada Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a traffic collision in La Mirada takes a family member's life, the grief is immediate, but the legal steps often feel confusing and rushed. Los Angeles County recorded traffic deaths on La Mirada's streets, including corridors like Valley View Avenue and La Mirada Boulevard where crash volumes are notably tracked. California law gives surviving spouses, domestic partners, and children the first right to pursue a wrongful death claim, with other dependents or heirs able to step in under certain circumstances. These claims are separate from any criminal charges the driver may face and focus instead on the financial and emotional losses left behind. Our team reviews the circumstances surrounding your loss, walks you through eligibility, deadlines, and what evidence matters. There's no upfront cost, and no fee unless we recover compensation on your behalf. You shouldn't have to sort through legal deadlines alone while mourning.

whyChoose.title: Why La Mirada Families Choose Us

items.title: Understanding Who Can File
items.desc: California limits standing to spouses, domestic partners, and children first, with dependents or other heirs eligible in certain situations. We can clarify where your family fits before time runs short.

items.title: Awareness of the Filing Deadline
items.desc: Wrongful death claims generally must be filed within two years of the date of death, though claims against a government entity carry a much shorter window. Missing that deadline can end a claim before it starts.

items.title: Contingency-Based Representation
items.desc: We work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless we recover compensation for your family. That removes upfront financial pressure during an already difficult time.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Typically, a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children have first priority to bring the claim. If none of those exist, other dependents or heirs may be eligible under specific circumstances. We can review your family's situation to confirm standing.

items.question: How does this differ from a criminal case against the driver?
items.answer: A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action focused on financial and emotional losses, not criminal punishment. The two cases can proceed independently, even if a criminal case results in no charges. Families can still pursue civil recovery regardless of the criminal outcome.

items.question: Does La Mirada's crash data affect my case?
items.answer: Public crash records showing collisions along corridors like Imperial Highway or Rosecrans Avenue can provide helpful context, though every case depends on its specific facts. These records aren't used to label any road as unsafe, but they can support the broader circumstances surrounding a claim. We can explain how such records might be relevant to your situation.
